plants.name: Prunus yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous tree that produces masses of delicate, fragrant, five-petaled blossoms before its leaves emerge. It is the most famous cherry tree used for hanami (flower viewing) celebrations and is widely planted in parks and along streets.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in Japan; blooms in mid to late March in warmer areas like Kyushu and Shikoku
plants.location: Japan (Kyushu, Shikoku, southern Honshu), Washington D.C. (USA) in late March, and Korea
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry trees along the Tidal Basin in Washington D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and the National Cherry Blossom Festival is timed to their peak bloom.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals. It grows in woodlands and meadows and is the parent of many cultivated daffodil varieties.
plants.location: Western Europe including the UK, France, and Belgium; naturalized in North American gardens and lawns
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain toxic alkaloids such as lycorine, and one compound, galantamine, is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A sub-tropical tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into clouds of lavender-blue, trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere autumn it can have a second, lighter bloom, while in some warmer regions it flowers sporadically.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (October to December) in the Southern Hemisphere, with occasional secondary flowering in early autumn; in the Northern Hemisphere tropics it blooms around March to May
plants.location: Native to South America; cultivated in Mexico City, Southern California, India, and parts of Africa where March to April blooming occurs
plants.funFact: Mexico City's streets turn purple each spring when thousands of jacaranda trees bloom, a sight that began after Japanese gardener Tatsugoro Matsumoto planted them in the early 20th century.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A large Himalayan tree that bears enormous, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches before the leaves appear. The blooms can reach up to 25 cm across and are among the showiest of all magnolias.
plants.location: Himalayas (Nepal, Bhutan, Sikkim, Yunnan), and cultivated in mild gardens in Cornwall, the Pacific Northwest, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: A magnolia seedling may take 20 to 30 years to flower for the first time, and the genus is so ancient that its flowers evolved before bees existed and are pollinated by beetles.
